questions.q: Which set lists the aggregate functions covered in this lesson?
options: COUNT, SUM, MEDIAN, MODE, RANGE
COUNT, TOTAL, MEAN, LOW, HIGH
SUM, ROUND, TOP, BOTTOM, FIRST
COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX
questions.explain: SOQL supports COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX, plus COUNT_DISTINCT.

questions.q: What is the difference between COUNT() and COUNT(Email)?
options: COUNT(Email) counts the characters in the Email field
COUNT() returns the number of matching rows, while COUNT(Email) counts only rows where Email is not null
They always return the same number
COUNT() counts only null values
questions.explain: COUNT() counts matching rows, like COUNT(*) in T-SQL. COUNT(field) skips rows where the field is null.

questions.q: How do you alias an aggregate in SOQL?
options: SUM(Amount) AS totalAmount is required
Aliases are not supported in SOQL
Use square brackets, as in SUM(Amount)[totalAmount]
Place the alias directly after the function, as in SUM(Amount) totalAmount, with no AS keyword
questions.explain: SOQL aliases follow the function directly with no AS. Without an alias, columns are named expr0, expr1, and so on.

questions.q: What kind of records does an aggregate query with GROUP BY or aggregate fields return, and how does Apex read the values?
options: Standard Opportunity records with extra fields
A single string with comma-separated values
The query returns nothing until it is saved
AggregateResult records, read by alias, such as ar.get('totalAmount')
questions.explain: Aggregate queries return AggregateResult records. Values are read by alias, or by expr0, expr1 if there is no alias.

questions.q: Why does SELECT StageName, COUNT(Id) FROM Opportunity fail without a GROUP BY?
options: StageName is not a valid Opportunity field
COUNT cannot be used on the Id field
A plain field mixed with an aggregate needs GROUP BY so SOQL knows how to group the rows
Aggregates can only run on custom objects
questions.explain: Mixing a plain field with an aggregate requires GROUP BY, which is covered in the next lesson.
